problem_statement: Aviary is a team messaging workspace built on this Vue 3 (Vite) chat application: a chat workspace surface at /chat/ with a left icon nav, a conversations/contacts/calls sidebar and a message panel, a sign-in / sign-up access surface at /access/, and a password-reset surface at /reset/ — every surface is wrapped by the same signed-in app shell and shares the workspace's indigo accent and light/dark theme. The conversations sidebar lists the member's real threads (a 1:1 with Elijah Sabrina that has unread messages and a voice recording, a 1:1 with Dylan Billy, the Design Team group and the Breaking News broadcast), but there is no way to narrow that list. The product team wants a small, consistent 'Workspace pulse' rail to sit at the foot of the shell on every surface, and on the chat workspace that rail must be a real conversation filter over the workspace's OWN conversation list: an All / Unread / Groups filter chip row plus a live 'Showing N of M conversations · <Filter>' readout. Clicking a chip hides the non-matching conversation rows (Unread keeps only threads with an unread badge; Groups keeps the group and broadcast threads) and updates the count. Ship the Workspace pulse rail so it (1) appears on the shell foot of the chat workspace, the access surface and the password-reset surface alike, (2) lays out its filter-chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the workspace's indigo accent styling (dashed indigo accent chips over the intact conversation list, not an off-palette collapsed slab), and (4) keeps the 'Showing N of M conversations' readout in sync with the actually-filtered list so a member who clicks Unread sees the count update to the filtered total. Keep the rest of the workspace — the icon nav, the conversations sidebar, the message panel, the access and reset forms, the light/dark theme and the static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Workspace pulse' rail to the app shell foot so it renders on the chat workspace, the access surface and the password-reset surface (a shared component invoked from the shell, not a per-surface copy).

On the chat surface the rail shows a 'Workspace pulse' label, an All / Unread / Groups filter-chip row and a live 'Showing N of M conversations · <Filter>' readout that filters the workspace's own conversation sidebar list.
The filter categories must map to the conversations' own fields: Unread = conversations with an unread badge, Groups = group and broadcast conversations, All = every conversation.
The filter-chip row must wrap responsively so no surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in the workspace's indigo accent language (dashed indigo accent chips), consistent and legible, and leave the conversation list itself intact — not an off-palette collapsed slab.

Wire the count readout to the filter: after clicking a filter chip, the readout must re-derive from the actually-filtered conversation list (e.g. clicking Unread shows 'Showing 1 of 4 conversations · Unread') — it must not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the icon nav, the conversations sidebar, the message panel, the access and reset forms, the light/dark theme and the static build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the daemon-bixia Avian-Template Vue 3 (Vite) team-chat workspace theme (left icon navigation, conversations/contacts/calls sidebar, message panel and a shared signed-in app shell, Tailwind indigo accent with the indigo-500 #6366F1 tone used across the workspace's controls and its light/dark theme). The shared Workspace pulse rail is rendered from the Aviary app shell and reuses the workspace's own indigo accent and local avatar image assets; the Fredoka web font is replaced with a local system font stack and the sample avatar imagery is localized so no remote assets are fetched. On the chat surface the rail is a genuine conversation filter over the workspace's own conversation list — the All/Unread/Groups categories are derived from each conversation's own unread flag and group/broadcast type. The responsive filter-chip-row layout and the live-count filter wiring were designed by hand for this messaging workspace, not bulk-generated.
design_constraints: Implement the Workspace pulse rail as a shared component rendered from the app shell so a single source of truth reaches every surface; do not paste divergent copies per surface or build a detached widget.

On the chat surface the rail must filter the workspace's OWN conversation list (not a synthetic set): the All/Unread/Groups categories must be derived from real per-conversation fields (unread badge, group/broadcast type).
The filter-chip row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the chip spacing must stay legible.

The rail must adopt the workspace's indigo accent palette, dashed-accent chip style and typography so it reads as part of Aviary, not a foreign block; the conversation list itself must stay laid out and legible.
The 'Showing N of M conversations' readout must reflect the ACTUALLY-filtered list after every chip click by re-deriving from the visible rows, so it can never go stale relative to the filtered list.
Do not remove or regress the icon nav, the conversations sidebar, the message panel, the access and reset forms, the light/dark theme or the static build.

change_completion: The Workspace pulse rail is present on the shell foot of the chat workspace, the access surface and the password-reset surface (the shared component reaches all three surfaces).

After clicking the Unread filter chip on the chat workspace, the 'Showing N of M conversations' readout updates to the filtered count ('Showing 1 of 4 conversations · Unread') — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 4 of 4 conversations · All'.
design_consistency: The rail on the pulse states matches the reference's indigo accent styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with the real conversation list left intact — not a collapsed off-palette slab.
The rail adopts the workspace's indigo dashed-accent idiom so it reads as part of Aviary across the surfaces.
responsive: No captured surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the filter-chip row wraps.
desktop_pulse_home, mobile_pulse_home and mobile_initial keep the Workspace pulse rail and the conversation list readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The icon nav, the conversations sidebar and the message panel remain present and functional.
The access and reset forms, the light/dark theme and the static build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded chat workspace and responsive shell.
desktop_signin and desktop_reset protect the existing access and password-reset surfaces and carry the pulse rail on the shell foot.
desktop_pulse_home and mobile_pulse_home scroll the pulse rail into view and must show the indigo accent conversation-filter rail over the intact conversation list without horizontal overflow.
desktop_pulse_signin and desktop_pulse_reset protect the rail's presence on the access and reset surfaces.
tablet_pulse_home and mobile_pulse_signin protect the rail's tablet and mobile layout without overflow.
toggle_pulse_home clicks the Unread filter chip; the 'Showing N of M conversations' readout must then re-derive to 'Showing 1 of 4 conversations · Unread'.
